claims.text: The target alloy is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
A reactive Ti getter in argon, with heating at 10 °C/min, can reduce oxygen to below 10 ppm.
The Ti getter scavenges oxygen by forming stable TiO2.
TaH0.5, NbH, HfH2, TiH2, and ZrH2 undergo sequential thermal decomposition during heating.
The critical decomposition window for the hydrides is approximately 400-900 °C.
Oxygen that must be scavenged originates from hydride decomposition and ambient leaks.
Maintaining low oxygen chemical potential prevents alpha-HCP nucleation in HfNbTaTiZr.
An equimolar five-component alloy has an ideal configurational entropy of mixing equal to Rln5.
High configurational entropy stabilizes a disordered BCC phase in equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Rapid quenching suppresses diffusion-limited decomposition into alpha-BCC and beta-BCC phases.
Rapid quenching from the homogenization temperature traps a metastable single-phase beta-BCC HfNbTaTiZr solid solution.
Slow cooling of the alloy produces a dual-phase alpha-BCC plus beta-BCC structure.
The proposed regime yields a nearly fully dense microstructure.
The quenched alloy has a grain size below 5 µm.
The quenched alloy contains negligible alpha-HCP and intermetallic phases.
A solid-solution atomic-size difference of δ ≤ 4.3% is a single-phase stability limit.
Sintering without a reactive getter, or with Zr treated as a passive getter, typically causes oxygen contamination, alpha-HCP formation, and a dual-BCC structure after slow cooling.
Detection of alpha-Ti or alpha-HCP diffraction peaks during 400-900 °C or after quenching demonstrates failure of the Ti getter to suppress alpha-phase nucleation.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis says heating to 1100 °C is followed by water quenching, whereas the intervention specifies quenching from a homogenization temperature of approximately 1200-1300 °C. The conditions field does not clearly state the additional ramp or hold between 1100 °C and the homogenization temperature.

The material initial state describes Ti getter powder as mixed with the precursor blend, while the intervention describes an atmosphere containing a Ti getter. An internally mixed Ti getter could alter the equiatomic Ti content, whereas an external sacrificial getter would not.
